newsitem.title: USA: Fire kills one, injures 24 at Mass. old age home.
newsitem.headline: Fire kills one, injures 24 at Mass. old age home.

text.p: An early morning fire consumed a public housing project for the elderly and handicapped Thursday, killing one and injuring 24 others, fire officials said.
The three-alarm blaze in this resort town on the tip of Cape Cod started shortly after 2:30 a.m. and quickly consumed the three-story wooden structure, fire officials said.

Rescue workers, some from communities up to 25 miles away, battled the fire. One woman who was severely injured was flown to Massachusetts General Hospital in Boston, 40 miles away by air, where she was listed in critical condition.
Ambulances took six others including a police officer and two firefighters to Cape Cod Community Hospital in Hyannis. The other injured were treated at the scene or a local clinic.
The dead woman was identified as Mira Cabral, who officials said was in her early 70s.
Provincetown Deputy Fire Chief Warren Alexander said the fire "has been ruled an accident" but he said state fire officials were still investigating the blaze.

The public housing project, in which rents for the elderly and handicapped were subsidized by the state, was built in 1986 without a sprinkler system, which was not required at the time, fire officials said.
